saratoga-springs.lead_heading: A Saratoga Springs league, organized by two friends
intro_paragraphs: Mahjong Springs is based in Saratoga Springs, Utah. Friends Lyndsey and Denise started the league so neighbors could play organized American Mahjong without having to assemble a foursome from scratch every week. An eight-week season is $80 to join, and players who live in Saratoga Springs are welcome—whether you are new to the National Mah Jongg League card or have been playing for years.

The league is simple by design. You sign up online, appear on the season roster, and then either host a four-person table or use Find a Table to claim an open seat. There is no single mandatory night. Official sessions are four games, scores are confirmed by a tablemate, and standings are tracked on our leaderboard. At the end of the season, prizes go to top finishers.
saratoga-springs.drive_heading: On the northwest shore of Utah Lake
saratoga-springs.drive_body: Saratoga Springs sits on the northwest shore of Utah Lake, with Lehi just across the Jordan River and Eagle Mountain along Pony Express Parkway and SR-73. This is our home base (84045). You can join a table here in town, and any league player can host a four-game session in a Saratoga Springs home or local gathering spot.
local_paragraphs: When you host, you choose the day, time, general part of town, and table style—standard, beginner-friendly, mindful-quiet, or social. Your home address stays private until a player claims a seat, and everyone who joins receives a calendar invite and a reminder the day before. Bring your current NMJL card; the host provides the tile set, racks, and space.

Players from nearby cities are welcome too, and the same hosting tools work if you would rather open a table closer to a friend. Hosting is optional. We offer a full refund if you cancel before a league starts; once the season begins, registrations are non-refundable.

faq.q: Where is Mahjong Springs based?
faq.a: In Saratoga Springs, Utah 84045, on the northwest shore of Utah Lake. The league was founded here by Lyndsey and Denise.

faq.q: Can I host a table in Saratoga Springs?
faq.a: Yes. Any rostered league player can host a four-person table in a home or local gathering spot in Saratoga Springs. You list the general part of town when you post the table, and your exact address is shared only with the players who join.

faq.q: What does the $80 season fee cover?
faq.a: Your $80 registration covers the full eight-week season, access to Find a Table and table hosting, score tracking on the season leaderboard, and eligibility for end-of-season prizes.

faq.q: What is the refund policy?
faq.a: We offer a full refund before a league starts. Once the season has begun, registrations are non-refundable.

faq.a: No. A host’s home address is visible only to the players who actually join that table, and your mobile number is shared with tablemates only if you choose to enable phone sharing on your profile.

payson-santaquin.lead_heading: A season that welcomes the south end of the county
intro_paragraphs: Payson sits south of Salem along I-15, near Payson Canyon and Mount Nebo. Santaquin is farther south still, at the south end of Utah County, where the interstate continues toward Juab County. These are the farthest Utah County cities we list, and players from both are welcome in Mahjong Springs eight-week American Mahjong leagues.

The league is based in Saratoga Springs and was founded by Lyndsey and Denise. A season is $80 for eight weeks. You do not need a ready-made foursome to join: sign up, then host a table in Payson or Santaquin, or use Find a Table to claim an open seat. All skill levels are welcome.
payson-santaquin.drive_heading: The longest drive from our home city
payson-santaquin.drive_body: Payson and Santaquin are at the south end of Utah County, so the trip from Saratoga Springs is the longest of our service areas—generally toward Lehi and then south on I-15 through Orem, Provo, Springville, and Spanish Fork. We are honest about that distance. The practical way to play, for many sessions, is to host a four-person table in Payson or Santaquin so neighbors can gather closer to home.
local_paragraphs: An official league session is four games from the current National Mah Jongg League card. The host provides the tile set and space; you bring your card. Hosts pick the day, time, general part of town, and table style, and a home address is shown only to the players who join that table. A calendar invite and a reminder go out before the session.

Scores are entered on your phone after the fourth game and confirmed by a tablemate. Standings are tracked on our leaderboard, and prizes go to top finishers, with recognition for consistency and frequent play. Hosting is optional. We offer a full refund if you cancel before a league starts; once the season begins, registrations are non-refundable.

faq.q: Santaquin is at the south end of the county. Are we included?
faq.a: Yes. Players from Santaquin and Payson are welcome to join any season, claim an open seat, or host a table locally.

faq.q: Do I have to drive to Saratoga Springs for every game?
faq.a: No. This is the longest drive from our home city of any area we list, and you are not expected to make that trip every session. Any league player can host a table in Payson or Santaquin.

faq.q: When do new seasons open?
faq.a: We run eight-week seasonal leagues, including Winter and Spring. Check the open and upcoming leagues listed on this page, or subscribe to The Table Talk Letter on our home page to hear when sign-ups open.

faq.q: Do I need to own a mahjong tile set to join?
faq.a: No. Hosts provide the tile set and space for the table; you only need to bring your own current NMJL card when you attend a session.
